messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? That might refer to the standard error of the mean under the null hypothesis? Usually we compute the standard error: sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). But they mention "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" maybe they want the standard error of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under the null hypothesis. That would be sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size) = 1.4 / sqrt(40). Let's compute: sqrt(40) ≈ 6.3249. 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2213. So standard error ≈ 0.2213.

But the user might want to calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? They might want to compute the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under the null hypothesis. That is indeed the standard error. So answer: 0.2213.

But the user might want to use the function to calculate p-value? They ask "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test". That is not a p-value. They might want to compute the standard error. So we can compute manually. There's no tool needed. So we can just provide the answer.

We should respond with the standard deviation (standard error) of the sampling distribution: 0.2213.

We can also mention that it's computed as sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). Provide the numeric result.

Thus answer: 0.2213.
